title: Distance to bank as IV for savings rate

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Two–Stage Least Squares (2SLS) Instrumental‐Variables (IV) estimation.  

Why IV?  
• Endogeneity concern: households that decide to open an account (x) may differ systematically in unobservables (e.g. patience, financial literacy) that also affect savings (y).  
• Instrument: distance to nearest bank branch (z). Greater distance makes having an account less likely but, conditional on controls, should not affect savings except through account ownership.

Key assumptions  
1. Relevance: Cov(z, x | controls) ≠ 0 – distance strongly predicts account ownership (first-stage F > 10).  
2. Exclusion: Conditional on controls, distance influences savings only via account ownership (no direct or omitted-variable channel).  
3. Independence: Distance is as-good-as randomly assigned with respect to unobserved determinants of savings after conditioning on controls.  

## 2. R Code
```r
#############################################################
#  Instrumental-Variables estimation: Bank account → Savings
#############################################################
# Required libraries
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(AER)        # ivreg
  library(sandwich)   # robust vcov
  library(lmtest)     # coeftest
})

# 1. Read data
dat <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s20_data.csv")

# Quick data check
cat("Observations:", nrow(dat), "\n\n")

# 2. First stage: does distance predict account ownership?
fs   <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = dat)
fs_F <- summary(fs)$fstatistic[1]
cat("First-stage F-statistic on instrument (rule-of-thumb > 10):", round(fs_F,2), "\n\n")

# 3. Second stage / IV estimate
iv_mod <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = dat)

# Robust (HC1) standard errors
robust_se <- vcovHC(iv_mod, type = "HC1")
iv_res    <- coeftest(iv_mod, vcov = robust_se)

# 4. Reduced form (distance → savings)
rf <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = dat)
rf_robust <- coeftest(rf, vcov = vcovHC(rf, type = "HC1"))

# 5. Print key numerical results
cat("=============== IV Estimate =================\n")
print(iv_res["x", ])         # coefficient, SE, t, p-value
cat("=============================================\n\n")

cat("Reduced-form effect of distance (z) on savings (y):\n")
print(rf_robust["z", ])

# 6. Diagnostics & robustness
cat("\n**************** Diagnostics ****************\n")
print(summary(iv_mod, diagnostics = TRUE)$diagnostics)

# Robustness check 1: add quadratic distance term
dat$z2 <- dat$z^2
iv_mod_quad <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + z2 + controls, data = dat)
quad_res    <- coeftest(iv_mod_quad, vcov = vcovHC(iv_mod_quad, type = "HC1"))
cat("\nIV with z and z^2 as instruments (checking sensitivity):\n")
print(quad_res["x", ])

# Robustness check 2: drop top/bottom 5% distance observations
p05 <- quantile(dat$z, 0.05)
p95 <- quantile(dat$z, 0.95)
trim  <- subset(dat, z >= p05 & z <= p95)
iv_trim <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = trim)
trim_res <- coeftest(iv_trim, vcov = vcovHC(iv_trim, type = "HC1"))
cat("\nIV after trimming extreme distance values:\n")
print(trim_res["x", ])
#############################################################
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Positive. Households with a bank account are expected to save more because accounts lower transaction costs, provide commitment devices, and yield interest.  

Magnitude: With monthly savings measured in USD and the (standardised) preview showing a standard deviation ≈ 1, an economically plausible IV estimate is around +0.4 to +0.7 (roughly one-half standard deviation increase in savings for account holders). The first-stage coefficient on distance should be negative (≈ -0.20 to ‑0.30 per km if z is continuous, or ≈ -0.3 if z is a near/far dummy), delivering a strong F-statistic comfortably above 10.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV/2SLS — instrument: branch distance; first stage: distance → account ownership (negative)
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Bank account ownership significantly increases savings
_ground_truth.main_effect: Having an account increases monthly savings by ~40% (IV estimate)
